caption: Model diagram of PatchRot. The input image is split into patches; the image and its patches are rotated by a random multiple of 90 degrees (0/90/180/270). A ViT is trained with new MLP heads to predict the rotation angle of the whole image (via the class token) and of each patch (via patch heads). Dotted lines denote shared weights.

Classification accuracies for (a) CIFAR-10, (b) CIFAR-100, (c) FashionMNIST and (d) Tiny-ImageNet for Supervised, RotNet and PatchRot. The x-axis (NF, PE, EB1-EB7, MLP) denotes which part of the ViT is fine-tuned while earlier layers are frozen.
Sample attention maps of a ViT trained with PatchRot on the Tiny-ImageNet validation set. Upper row: input image; lower row: attention map. The model attends to the salient object.

Top-5 classification accuracy versus number of PatchRot pretraining epochs for CIFAR-100. More self-supervised pretraining steadily improves downstream accuracy across fine-tuning depths (NF, EB5, MLP) relative to the supervised baseline.
PatchRot in a transfer-learning setting: (a) CIFAR100->CIFAR10 and (b) CIFAR10->CIFAR100. PatchRot self-supervised pretraining on the source dataset transfers better than supervised pretraining.
